brief: The wind became a scalar at #58 and it changed nothing on screen, because `windyDay()` is a day hash and the ramp starts at the hour-6 roll — inside the dawn relight, the one hour nobody can see it (c96). Give the wind a cause: let the wind target rise with a building front — `cloudCover()` climbs over ~half a day before rain and breaks after it — so on a front day the washing, bunting, fountain, river and smoke all pick up mid-morning or mid-afternoon as the sky darkens, and drop when the rain breaks. Keep the day hash as a second source (a dry windy day still exists) and keep `stepWind`'s rate cap so nothing steps. Show it: a fountain or washing-line crop series across a front's build (flat light, hour 10–14), Δ/frame rising smoothly; `wind-year.mjs` windy-day mean and calm mean stated before and after; the windy CLASS fraction of hours before and after (it will rise — say by how much).
successLooksLike: On a seed with a mid-day front, a 4-shot crop series at hour 10–14 shows the fountain jets leaning progressively as the sky darkens; calm-day frames identical to HEAD; the boat and fountain anchors move only by the extra windy hours, and the ledger says how many.
avoid: Do not add an R() draw. Do not touch the consumers — they read windF() and that is the point. Do not let the wind stay up through the rain itself unless you can show a shower on HEAD already has the washing brought in.
